newsitem.title: USA: Regulator rejects Primergy merger, urges new plan.
newsitem.headline: Regulator rejects Primergy merger, urges new plan.

text.p: Federal energy regulators Wednesday rejected the planned $6 billion merger of Northern States Power Co. and Wisconsin Energy Corp. and gave the companies three months to work out an acceptable plan.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, in rejecting the deal as it was proposed, overruled a finding by an administrative law judge that the utilities' plans for independent power systems would resolve concerns about competition in Wisconsin and upper Michigan.
"We are resolute that we cannot determine that mergers that increase market power to unacceptable levels are in the public interest," FERC Chairman Elizabeth Moler said.
The $6 billion merger of the upper Midwest utilities into a new holding company called Primergy Corp. would have created the nation's 10th-largest utility.

The commission ordered the companies to try to work out an acceptable plan and suggested that selling some generating capacity could address concerns about competition. "In the three months coming, the parties are being sent away to get this right," FERC Commissioner James Hoecker said.
Separately, Wisconsin Energy agreed to buy Eselco Inc., which owns two electric utilities, for $71 million in stock, the companies said Wednesday.
